title: Launcher & interface
summary: Update your game and use Nightcap’s custom interface.
body:
Launch repair published: Game update 2026101901 corrects the client catalog mismatch that blocked Play after the previous update. Close EverQuest and the launcher, reopen your normal Nightcap shortcut, and press Play to receive the repair. Your game settings and the other managed files are preserved. Native login and gameplay confirmation remain open.

Live testing: Game update 2026101802 pairs the expanded pet Equipment tab and spell/AA descriptions with the new server release. Close EverQuest and use the normal launcher before testing. The Classic travel repairs remain included.

Classic travel file checks

Game update 2026101801 adds terrain and object archive checks for 17 Classic travel destinations, including West Commonlands, Misty Thicket and Toxxulia. Fully close EverQuest, reopen your usual launcher, select the game folder you actually use, and press Play. Missing or corrupted managed files are downloaded before the game starts; matching files are reused. Your settings are preserved. This covers the listed managed archives, not every file in a RoF2 installation. Report the exact error if a zone still fails after updating.

One shortcut and automatic updates

Your usual Nightcap shortcut updates the launcher and game before Play. For the new loading gallery, fully close both the game and launcher, then reopen that shortcut. Keep your existing game folder; another game installation can stay running during an update.

Read each release’s changes

The launcher shows dated Feature and Bug fix summaries for the current update, plus expandable previous patches. Close the game and launcher, then reopen your usual shortcut when updating. Use Features for the current systems and Recent changes for the wiki’s release history.

The Nightcap interface loads automatically

Class labels, the ability Class column, and custom pet and loot controls load with the game. Background interface requests no longer clutter local chat.

Spellbook, spell gems, and mana for your build

A melee starting class can use the spellbook and spell gems when your held classes provide spell access. The mana gauge follows your actual mana pool.

Classic character and creature appearances

Supported older models are used where available, including original elemental colors. Creatures without an older counterpart retain their appearance. The game’s model configuration also supports opting into modern appearances; a full restart is required.

Ten original paintings across the loading gallery

All 55 numbered loading screens and the fallback now use ten original Nightcap paintings, including the SoulFire Paladin and the gnome with three pets. The launcher installs the complete gallery while preserving your settings.

Startup and character-selection repairs

Updates repair model archives and missing materials behind the recent Play and character-selection failures. Install through the usual launcher; no reinstall is needed.

Creature and pet animation repairs

The latest updates repair shared creature animations and Enchanter weapon-pet identity. Beetle walking and death were confirmed fixed; pet motion and wider visual checks continue.

October 17 gameplay update

Close EverQuest and choose Play to receive the Recommended AA window and independent Monk attack timers. Latest update lists these changes with death EXP, stack limits, reforging and reliability improvements. Previous patches retains the dungeon launch notes.
